title: Try the A1 Writing Tasks with Short Clocks

lessons.title: Three lines from two old cards
lessons.gloss: choose three already taught form values from separate card marks

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: The old fictional A, ਕ and B, ਖ cards are familiar. A form can choose a different old card for each line. The mark tells you which known value to retrieve; it is not a new word or a new person to memorise.

Reopen the two old value banks for this rehearsal only. Read one label and its mark, select the taught value, then cover that line before moving to the next. There is no clock and no independent writing credit in this supported step.
Check only card selection first. Then check spelling and the space after each colon in a separate pass. The next lesson will close the banks and use all six familiar labels.
Close both banks after the supported check.

segments.prompt: With the old A and B banks visible, fill name from A, language from B, and residence from A.
acceptedResponses: ਨਾਂ: ਅਮਨ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ: ਹਿੰਦੀ ਰਿਹਾਇਸ਼: ਪਿੰਡ

feedback.correct: Each known value followed its own card mark.
feedback.incorrect: Check one label and one card mark at a time, then check the Gurmukhi spacing.

lessons.title: A short clock for six known fields
lessons.gloss: fill six taught Gurmukhi form fields from a new mix of familiar card marks under a short clock

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Close the old cards. Keep a blank page and a three-minute timer. The six marks below mix familiar values; no model is shown.

Start the three-minute timer. Retrieve each marked value and write all six fields in Gurmukhi, with Gurmukhi digits for age and phone. Stop on time and leave unfinished lines as evidence. Keep models and aids closed.
Record completed lines and elapsed seconds. After the timer, check values, spelling, spacing, digit order, and phone grouping separately. Preserve the first attempt; repair is not timed evidence.
This short checkpoint is not the full A1 paper. Two complete mocks test the twenty-minute form-plus-message condition.

segments.prompt: With the old banks closed, start a three-minute timer and complete the six Gurmukhi fields from these marks in order: name A, language B, residence A, work B, age A, phone B. Stop at the timer.
acceptedResponses: ਨਾਂ: ਅਮਨ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ: ਹਿੰਦੀ ਰਿਹਾਇਸ਼: ਪਿੰਡ ਕੰਮ: ਨੌਕਰੀ ਉਮਰ: ੧੫ ਫ਼ੋਨ: ੦੨੫ ੧੨੫

feedback.correct: All six taught values were retrieved and placed under the short clock.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the timed first attempt; later repair one field or script dimension at a time.

lessons.title: Pace the first two message chunks
lessons.gloss: rehearse a small timed part before the full named-reader message checkpoint

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: The whole A1 writing paper lasts twenty minutes. Its message is 30–40 words for one named reader and purpose. Today you will time only a small opening, not pretend to fit that whole paper into a short lesson.

Close the earlier message pages. Imagine Aman writing to Manan. In ninety seconds, make two familiar chunks: a greeting that names Manan, then one wellbeing question. You may choose the exact taught words and punctuation; no sample sentence is visible here. Stop at ninety seconds and record the number of words you produced.
After the timer, check only whether Manan is clearly the reader. Next check the question mark and spacing. Repairing after the clock helps learning but does not change the recorded first attempt.
The next checkpoint uses a fresh purpose, a full 30–40-word message, and a short clock. The old supported message lacks the required water detail, so copying its old order would miss that purpose.

lessons.title: A new message under a short clock
lessons.romanization: Aman writes Manan with a new purpose
lessons.gloss: write a thirty-to-forty-word Gurmukhi message under a short clock without a model

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Close all earlier message pages. Set a three-minute timer and keep a blank page. The task below uses known language, but the reader, speaker, and purpose combination is not the old independent note. No romanization, sentence bank, or copyable answer is available while the clock runs.

As Aman, write Manan a 30–40-word Gurmukhi message. Greet Manan and ask about his wellbeing. Say that you like water and one other familiar thing. Then suggest meeting again and close in a fitting tone. You may add other already taught words to reach the band. Choose and order your own sentences; the old supported Aman-to-Manan model did not include the water purpose.

Start the timer. Stop at three minutes, even if unfinished. Record the word count and elapsed time on a separate line. Do not use a dictionary, translator, spell-checker, or earlier page during this first attempt.

Before reopening anything, note whether the named reader, water detail, meeting purpose, and 30–40-word band are present. Keep the first attempt unchanged. Repair comes in the next short lesson, not inside the timed score.
This short message checkpoint is timed writing evidence, not a complete twenty-minute A1 paper. The two full mocks and human validation remain separate gates to readiness.

lessons.title: Repair without rewriting the clock
lessons.romanization: inspect timed evidence without changing it
lessons.gloss: repair task fulfilment, order, Punjabi control, and Gurmukhi orthography in separate passes

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Keep the original timed form and message unchanged. Copy neither into a new scored answer. The clock showed what you could produce then; this short lesson shows what one careful repair can teach next.

First inspect task fulfilment: six requested form values, one named reader, the requested message details, and a 30–40-word message. Then inspect order: each value beside its own label, and greeting, content, invitation, and close in a readable sequence. Third, inspect Punjabi vocabulary and grammar, including agreement and tone. Last, inspect Gurmukhi spelling, word spaces, punctuation, digit order, and phone grouping. Do one pass at a time.
Choose one error dimension and write one corrected line on a separate page. Say what changed. Do not present this later line as the timed response.
Record one next practice target for the form and one for the message. A full paper still asks for both tasks in twenty minutes; only the complete timed mocks can test that combined condition.

lessons.title: Return to two familiar form lines
lessons.romanization: a short return to the familiar form clock
lessons.gloss: retrieve mixed card values under a small practice clock, then repair separately

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: This is a short, unscored return to the form you already tried. Keep the original timed form unchanged. A new practice line cannot replace its evidence.
Close the old A, ਕ and B, ਖ value banks. Read each mark before recalling its value. Set a one-minute practice timer; it is not an A1 paper score.
Start the practice timer. Write these two known lines in Gurmukhi. Stop when the minute ends, even if a line is unfinished.

Only after stopping, check the old values: ਨਾਂ: ਅਮਨ and ਭਾਸ਼ਾ: ਹਿੰਦੀ. On a separate page, repair one missed value or one Gurmukhi spelling. Leave both the first practice lines and the earlier six-field timed form untouched.
Cover the checks.
Recall the order: read each card mark, write under the short practice clock, stop, then repair on another page. This return does not count as a complete form-and-message mock.

lessons.title: Check a second pair without changing the first attempt
lessons.gloss: retrieve two other known form values and check one repair dimension

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: The first timed six-field form still shows what happened then. This small return uses two other taught lines and keeps the later repair separate.
Close the old card banks.
Read the A, ਕ and B, ਖ marks aloud. Each mark chooses a familiar value, not a new person or word.
Use a one-minute practice timer. Write these two lines without a model, then stop. This is a retrieval rehearsal, not another scored checkpoint.

Check after the clock: ਰਿਹਾਇਸ਼: ਪਿੰਡ and ਕੰਮ: ਨੌਕਰੀ. If a value or letter slipped, write one corrected line on another page. Name the one thing you changed: card choice, Gurmukhi spelling, or spacing. Keep the clocked practice and the earlier timed form as they were.
Cover the answers.
Recall the two marked values, then say why a later corrected line must not be counted as the first timed response. Full form-and-message mocks and human review still lie ahead.

lessons.title: Return to the named reader and opening
lessons.romanization: return to the short named-reader message clock
lessons.gloss: retrieve a familiar greeting and wellbeing question for a named reader

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Keep the earlier three-minute message unchanged. This small rehearsal returns to its reader and first two chunks; it is not a second scored message.
Close earlier message pages. Recall the known reader, Manan, and the two opening jobs: greet him and ask about his wellbeing. Use known Punjabi only.

Set a one-minute practice timer. As Aman, write a Gurmukhi greeting to Manan and one wellbeing question. Stop when the minute ends. On a separate line, record whether the reader was named and the question ended with a question mark. Do not change the clocked lines while checking them.
If one element slipped, write one corrected line on another page. A later repair helps you learn, but it cannot replace either original timed attempt.
Cover your practice lines.
Say the two opening jobs in order and name the reader. The full message also needs its familiar purpose and close; the two complete A1 mocks have not been attempted here.

lessons.title: Return to the familiar message purpose
lessons.romanization: return to the short named-reader message purpose
lessons.gloss: rehearse a short whole message using only taught language

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: The earlier named-reader message remains the scored short checkpoint. This return practises its known jobs without adding a new task or a new word.
On a blank page, recall the order: Manan as reader, a greeting and wellbeing question, the familiar water detail, a meeting invitation, then a close. Keep earlier models closed.

Set a two-minute practice timer. As Aman, write a 30–40-word Gurmukhi message to Manan with those already taught details. Stop when the timer ends, even if the word band is unfinished. This is an unscored retrieval, not a full A1 paper or a replacement for the earlier independent checkpoint.

After stopping, record the word count. Check the named reader, water detail, meeting purpose, and close one at a time. Keep the clocked page unchanged; if needed, repair one line on another page and name what changed.
Cover both pages.
Recall the opening and purpose in order. Later full twenty-minute form-and-message mocks, followed by human review, are still required before a durable A1 writing claim.
